questions.q: Why do time intelligence functions need a dedicated date table?
options: They depend on a contiguous, gap-free sequence of dates, which a fact table's date column doesn't naturally provide
They only work with text-formatted dates
They require the date table to have no relationships
They only work in DirectQuery mode
questions.explain: A fact table only has rows for dates when something happened. Time intelligence functions need a table with one row for every day, whether or not there was activity.

options: Power BI's default behavior of automatically building hidden date tables and hierarchies for detected date columns
A setting that disables all date-related visuals
A manual process for entering dates one at a time
A feature only available in the Power BI service, not Desktop
questions.explain: Auto date/time is why drilling into Year, Quarter, Month, Day works on a date field without any setup — Power BI builds that structure automatically by default.

questions.q: What does Power BI check when validating a column you mark as a date table?
options: Unique values, no nulls, contiguous dates, and a consistent timestamp if it's a Date/Time type
That the column contains at least 1,000 rows
That the table has no relationships to any other table
That every date is in the current calendar year
questions.explain: These four rules ensure the date table can support every day-by-day calculation time intelligence functions need — gaps or duplicate dates break that guarantee.

questions.q: When must you explicitly mark a date table, rather than relying on auto date/time?
options: When the relationship to the date table uses a surrogate key column of a different data type than Date/Time
Only when the model has fewer than five tables
Auto date/time always covers every scenario — marking is never required
Only when using Power BI on a Mac
questions.explain: A common case: a data warehouse's fact table joins to its date table via a whole-number surrogate key (like 20241231), not an actual date column — auto date/time can't handle that, so you mark the table explicitly.

questions.q: What happens to a table's existing auto-generated date hierarchy when you mark it as a date table?
options: Power BI removes the built-in auto-generated date table, and any visuals/DAX relying on it may break
Nothing changes — both hierarchies coexist
The auto-generated hierarchy becomes read-only
It converts the column to a calculated column automatically
questions.explain: Marking a date table replaces the automatic one Power BI had built — which is why it's best done early, before building visuals or formulas that depend on the auto-generated version.
